accepted.s: Under the three-capitals arrangement provided by the Andhra Pradesh laws of 2020, which of the following was correctly associated with Visakhapatnam?
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam was designated as the executive capital, Amaravati as the legislative capital and Kurnool as the judicial capital.
accepted.tq: Test the functional distinction between the three proposed capitals.
accepted.sec: Capital city debate - Amaravati, three-capitals laws and their repeal

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of Acts constituted the three-capitals legislative framework of Andhra Pradesh in 2020?
o: AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020
AP Regional Balance Act, 2020 and Kurnool Judicial Capital Act, 2020
AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and Six-Point Formula Act, 1973
AP Capital Development Act, 2019 and Amaravati Protection Act, 2021
accepted.x: The framework consisted of the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official names of paired enactments.
accepted.sec: Capital city debate - Amaravati, three-capitals laws and their repeal

accepted.s: Both the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020 were withdrawn in:
accepted.x: Both laws were withdrawn in November 2021.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the year of enactment and the year of withdrawal.
accepted.sec: Capital city debate - Amaravati, three-capitals laws and their repeal

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the post-2024 capital policy of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The coalition government has committed to completing Amaravati within three years.
2. It is pursuing a central law to protect Amaravati as the capital.
3. The proposed protection is being pursued through a Bill in Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct as of the reported position in January 2026.
accepted.tq: Check whether the statements describe the same policy initiative or alter its institutional route.
accepted.sec: Capital city debate - Amaravati, three-capitals laws and their repeal

accepted.s: Which organisation sought a special central package for Amaravati in the Union Budget 2026–27?
accepted.x: CII Andhra Pradesh sought a special central package for Amaravati in the Union Budget 2026–27.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation associated with the budget demand.
accepted.sec: Capital city debate - Amaravati, three-capitals laws and their repeal

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the political positions concerning the three-capitals proposal?
o: YSRCP argued that Amaravati spending hurts north coastal districts and drought-prone Rayalaseema, while the coalition feared revival of the three-capitals plan in 2029.
YSRCP supported Amaravati spending, while the coalition opposed its revival in 2029.
The coalition argued that Amaravati spending harms Telangana, while YSRCP favoured three capitals after 2029.
Both YSRCP and the coalition demanded that Kurnool be made the permanent capital.
accepted.x: YSRCP criticised large spending on Amaravati as harmful to north coastal districts and drought-prone Rayalaseema; the coalition feared that the three-capitals plan could be revived in 2029.
accepted.tq: Separate the positions of competing political actors rather than matching only one issue.
accepted.sec: Capital city debate - Amaravati, three-capitals laws and their repeal

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its pre-2022, 13-district regional grouping?
o: North Andhra — Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam
North Andhra — Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
Coastal Andhra — East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
Rayalaseema — Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
accepted.x: Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore were placed in Coastal Andhra, not North Andhra. The other three pairings are correct; Kadapa is also known as YSR district.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong regional grouping by checking the complete membership list.
accepted.sec: Regions of AP - Coastal Andhra, North Andhra (Uttarandhra), Rayalaseema

accepted.s: In the public-employment zonal grouping described for the pre-2022 regional structure, Zone II comprised:
o: East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna
accepted.x: Zone II comprised East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna. Zone I covered North Andhra, Zone III covered Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore, and Zone IV covered Rayalaseema.
accepted.tq: Distinguish regional grouping from the similarly numbered employment zone.
accepted.sec: Regions of AP - Coastal Andhra, North Andhra (Uttarandhra), Rayalaseema

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the public-employment zones is correct?
1. Zone I covered North Andhra.
2. Zone IV covered Rayalaseema.
3. Zones V and VI went to Telangana.
4. Hyderabad was included in Zone VI.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct in the stated six-zone arrangement.

accepted.s: The first session of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held on:
accepted.x: The first session of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held on 28 January 1934.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of an early regional organisation from the dates of later agreements.

accepted.s: Who presided over the first session of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha?
accepted.x: Nemali Pattabhirama Rao presided over the first session of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha.
accepted.tq: Match the office-holder with the organisation and event.
accepted.sec: Historical agreements - Sri Bagh Pact, Gentlemen's Agreement

accepted.s: The Rayalaseema Mahasabha demanded the establishment of a university at:
accepted.x: The Rayalaseema Mahasabha demanded a university at Tirupati.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific regional demand rather than the later university-centre arrangement.
accepted.sec: Historical agreements - Sri Bagh Pact, Gentlemen's Agreement

accepted.s: The Sri Bagh Pact was signed on 16 November 1937 at Sri Bagh, the residence of:
accepted.x: The pact was signed at Sri Bagh, the residence of K. Nageswara Rao of Andhra Patrika.
accepted.tq: Combine the date, venue and associated personality in one identification question.
accepted.sec: Historical agreements - Sri Bagh Pact, Gentlemen's Agreement

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Sri Bagh Pact?
o: Irrigation priority for Rayalaseema for ten years
Andhra University centres at Waltair and Anantapur
A cabinet ratio of 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana
accepted.x: The 60:40 cabinet ratio was a provision of the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956. The other provisions belonged to the Sri Bagh Pact.
accepted.tq: Separate provisions of two regional agreements by identifying the borrowed provision.
accepted.sec: Historical agreements - Sri Bagh Pact, Gentlemen's Agreement

accepted.s: Under the Sri Bagh Pact, the capital and High Court were to be divided between the regions, with the choice made first by:
accepted.x: Rayalaseema was given the first choice regarding the division of the capital and High Court between the regions.
accepted.tq: Test the exact beneficiary of a preference clause.
accepted.sec: Historical agreements - Sri Bagh Pact, Gentlemen's Agreement

accepted.s: When Andhra State was formed in 1953, the Sri Bagh arrangement resulted in:
o: The capital at Anantapur and High Court at Waltair
The capital at Guntur and High Court at Kurnool
The capital at Kurnool and High Court at Guntur
Both capital and High Court at Amaravati
accepted.x: The arrangement meant that Kurnool became the capital and Guntur became the seat of the High Court when Andhra State was formed in 1953.
accepted.tq: Use the reversal trap between the locations of the capital and High Court.
accepted.sec: Historical agreements - Sri Bagh Pact, Gentlemen's Agreement

accepted.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 primarily provided safeguards for:
o: North Andhra on the formation of Andhra State
Telangana on its merger to form Andhra Pradesh
Rayalaseema on its merger with Coastal Andhra
accepted.x: The Gentlemen's Agreement provided safeguards for Telangana when it merged with Andhra to form Andhra Pradesh in 1956.
accepted.tq: Identify the protected region and the constitutional-political context of the agreement.
accepted.sec: Historical agreements - Sri Bagh Pact, Gentlemen's Agreement

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. It provided for a 60:40 Andhra–Telangana cabinet ratio.
2. It created a Telangana Regional Committee.
3. It protected Telangana's surplus funds.
4. It included safeguards in jobs and education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four were safeguards or institutional provisions of the Gentlemen's Agreement.
accepted.tq: Check a multi-feature agreement by testing its institutional and financial safeguards together.
accepted.sec: Historical agreements - Sri Bagh Pact, Gentlemen's Agreement

accepted.s: Which of the following events is correctly placed in chronological order?
o: Separate Andhra flag hoisted — P. V. Narasimha Rao resigned — President's Rule began
P. V. Narasimha Rao resigned — separate Andhra flag hoisted — President's Rule began
President's Rule began — separate Andhra flag hoisted — P. V. Narasimha Rao resigned
Separate Andhra flag hoisted — President's Rule began — P. V. Narasimha Rao resigned
accepted.x: The separate Andhra flag was hoisted on 10 December 1972; P. V. Narasimha Rao resigned and President's Rule began on 18 January 1973.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence by comparing the two events dated in December 1972 and January 1973.
accepted.sec: Mulki rules and the Six-Point Formula - constitutional article, zonal system

accepted.s: The inclusion of Assistant Surgeons and Engineers under the Mulki rules in 1972 led directly to the:
accepted.x: The extension of Mulki rules to Assistant Surgeons and Engineers in 1972 sparked the Jai Andhra agitation.
accepted.tq: Link the immediate administrative cause to the resulting movement.
accepted.sec: Mulki rules and the Six-Point Formula - constitutional article, zonal system

accepted.s: President's Rule in Andhra Pradesh during the Jai Andhra crisis ran from:
accepted.x: President's Rule ran from 18 January 1973 to 10 December 1973.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the start and end dates of President's Rule from nearby movement dates.
accepted.sec: Mulki rules and the Six-Point Formula - constitutional article, zonal system

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Six-Point Formula of 1973?
o: Continuation of the Telangana Regional Committee
Local preference in non-gazetted posts and admissions
accepted.x: The Six-Point Formula abolished the Telangana Regional Committee. It provided for a Central University at Hyderabad, an Administrative Tribunal and local preference in specified posts and admissions.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversal of an institution that was abolished rather than continued.
accepted.sec: Mulki rules and the Six-Point Formula - constitutional article, zonal system

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Six-Point Formula of 1973?
o: Employee grievances — committee; backward areas — State Planning Board sub-committees
Employee grievances — Telangana Regional Committee; backward areas — District Courts
Employee grievances — Finance Commission; backward areas — Central University
Employee grievances — Mulki Tribunal; backward areas — Parliament committee
accepted.x: The formula provided a committee for employee grievances and State Planning Board sub-committees for backward areas.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and eliminate bodies not mentioned in the arrangement.
accepted.sec: Mulki rules and the Six-Point Formula - constitutional article, zonal system

accepted.s: The Six-Point Formula received constitutional backing through the insertion of:
accepted.x: The 32nd Amendment Act, 1973 inserted Articles 371D and 371E to provide constitutional backing for the Six-Point Formula.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among neighbouring constitutional article numbers.
accepted.sec: Mulki rules and the Six-Point Formula - constitutional article, zonal system

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Six-Point Formula approved
B. Telangana Regional Committee dissolved
C. Separate Andhra flag hoisted
D. Jai Andhra movement called off
accepted.x: The flag was hoisted on 10 December 1972; the formula was approved on 18 December 1973; the Telangana Regional Committee was dissolved on 1 January 1974. The Jai Andhra movement was called off on 1 October 1973, so the complete order is C, A, B, D only if interpreting the dates? Actually 1 October 1973 precedes 18 December 1973; therefore the correct chronological order is C, D, A, B.
accepted.tq: Compare all four dates rather than relying only on the broad sequence of the crisis.
accepted.sec: Mulki rules and the Six-Point Formula - constitutional article, zonal system

accepted.s: Under the Presidential Order of 1975, which of the following zonal arrangements was correct?
o: Zones I–III Rayalaseema, Zone IV Coastal Andhra, Zones V–VI North Andhra
Zone I Telangana, Zones II–IV Coastal Andhra, Zones V–VI Rayalaseema
Zones I–III Coastal Andhra, Zone IV Rayalaseema, Zones V–VI Telangana
Zones I–II Coastal Andhra, Zones III–IV Telangana, Zones V–VI Rayalaseema
accepted.x: The six-zone system placed Coastal Andhra in Zones I–III, Rayalaseema in Zone IV and Telangana in Zones V–VI; Hyderabad was in Zone VI.
accepted.tq: Compare the regional blocks with their zone ranges and reject the reversed arrangement.
accepted.sec: Mulki rules and the Six-Point Formula - constitutional article, zonal system

accepted.s: The Jai Andhra movement of 1972–73 was triggered by the Mulki rules and was called off on:

accepted.s: The Telangana movement of 2001–2014 culminated in the formation of Telangana on:
accepted.x: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 led to the formation of Telangana on 2 June 2014.
accepted.tq: Identify the statutory outcome and its effective date.

accepted.s: The principal grievance associated with the Telangana movement of 2001–2014 was:
o: Opposition to the creation of Zone IV
Non-implementation of the safeguards promised in 1956
Failure to establish a university at Tirupati
Demand for irrigation priority for Rayalaseema
accepted.x: The movement was associated with grievances over the unimplemented safeguards of 1956.
accepted.tq: Connect a later political movement with the earlier agreement whose safeguards were disputed.
accepted.sec: Separate-state movements - Jai Andhra, Telangana movements, Greater Rayalaseema

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Greater Rayalaseema demand?
o: It was not accepted, and the region remained in residuary Andhra Pradesh.
It was accepted through the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
It led to the creation of a fourth capital at Anantapur.
It resulted in Rayalaseema becoming a separate State in 1973.
accepted.x: The separate-state demand raised by Rayalaseema activists during the bifurcation debate was not accepted; Rayalaseema remained part of residuary Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test the actual outcome against plausible but unsupported institutional outcomes.
